detail.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable Hard Rules in `AGENTS.md`; the changes comply.
- [ ] Required labels: `cat-bugfix`, `area:linear_attention`, `orig-nv-eng` (maintainer help needed; my account cannot add labels).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: GDP summary normalization.

## Summary

Repeated GDP summary calls with token-major K and in-kernel L2 normalization fail because the cached normalization launch binds rank-4 K to a dummy Q argument compiled as rank 3. Pass the normalized-K workspace as that unused argument, matching the initial `skip_q=True` compilation.

Extend the existing token-major summary test to execute twice, preserving bitwise comparisons with expanded inputs for forward state, transition and backward summary.

## API and compatibility impact

None. The actual K input, normalization math, workspace and stream are unchanged.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --files python/cudnn/linear_attention/frost/gdn_engine.py test/python/linear_attention/test_la.py`: passed.
- On NVIDIA GB300, from `test/python`: `python -m pytest -q linear_attention/test_la.py::test_gdp_summary_token_major_bitwise`: **3 passed** (Householder counts 1, 2, 3).
- With the original engine line restored, the same regression fails at the cached L2-normalization launch with `Mismatched Tensor on argument #0 ... expected ndim=3`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected cached attention normalization to use the normalized key values consistently in the query-side calculation. This addresses an inconsistency in the cached path and improves the reliability of linear attention results. Other attention behavior is unchanged.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

files.patch:
@@ -3298,14 +3298,16 @@ def test_gdp_summary_token_major_bitwise(backend, n):
     k, v, beta, g, q = to_thd(case.k), to_thd(case.v), to_thd(case.gates["beta"]), to_thd(case.gates["g"]), to_thd(case.q)
     set_seed(SEED + 2)
     dO = torch.randn(case.T, case.HO, case.V, device="cuda").to(case.dtype)
-    with waive_unsupported(backend, "gdp"):
-        h_e, m_e = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary(k, v, g, beta, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
-        h_t, m_t = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary(k_tm, v_tm, g, beta_tm, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
-        g_e = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary_bwd(q, k, g, beta, dO, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
-        g_t = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary_bwd(q, k_tm, g, beta_tm, dO, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
-    assert_bitwise("H", h_t, h_e)
-    assert_bitwise("M", m_t, m_e)
-    assert_bitwise("G", g_t, g_e)
+    # Exercise both initial compilation and reuse of the cached summaries.
+    for _ in range(2):
+        with waive_unsupported(backend, "gdp"):
+            h_e, m_e = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary(k, v, g, beta, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
+            h_t, m_t = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary(k_tm, v_tm, g, beta_tm, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
+            g_e = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary_bwd(q, k, g, beta, dO, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
+            g_t = la_ops.gated_delta_product_summary_bwd(q, k_tm, g, beta_tm, dO, case.cu, n, use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True, plan_name="gdp_summary_frost")
+        assert_bitwise("H", h_t, h_e)
+        assert_bitwise("M", m_t, m_e)
+        assert_bitwise("G", g_t, g_e)
 
 
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("backend", ["frost"], indirect=True)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `1ce305be7358` against base `aba744cd66fd`.

Thank you for your contribution! The fix makes cached execution bind the same rank-3 placeholder as initial compilation. With skip_q=True, that argument is not read by the kernel; the actual K input and normalization are unchanged. No actionable findings.

Validation: Reviewed both changed files and the normalization build/run path, including the zero query-row count, token-major strides, workspace lifetime and stream forwarding. Current develop has no intervening change to the consumed linear-attention code. Precheck found no candidates; no kernel synchronization changed. On native SM100 with Torch 2.11 and public DSL 4.7, all three updated in-tree tests passed for Householder counts 1/2/3: initial and cached forward state/transition and backward summary match expanded inputs bitwise. Source and compatible extension provenance were verified. Four additional BF16/FP16 tests passed for counts 1/3 with ragged and empty sequences: CUDA Graph replay after changing input data, and eager reuse with new tensor addresses, match expanded-layout outputs bitwise. Independently undoing just the changed argument reproduces the original argument-0 rank mismatch for counts 1/2/3.

Limitations: This is focused native SM100 validation, not a complete linear-attention suite or independent SM103/SM107 qualification. The author's GB300 results remain separate evidence.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
